[strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-CAP-MAP-0.2.02.md#l1-capability-network-security]

## L1 Capability: Network Security

Network Security is the enterprise security capability that governs traffic flows between systems, services, users, and external networks — enforcing explicit access controls, traffic inspection, and segmentation at the network layer. In a Zero Trust architecture, the network is not a trust boundary but a transport medium: every traffic flow must be subject to policy evaluation regardless of source or destination. The Network Security capability provides the architectural constructs through which that policy evaluation is defined, deployed, and governed. It is a cross-cutting enforcement layer that interacts with the Identity, Endpoint, Application, and Data security capabilities to enable defense-in-depth across the enterprise technology estate.

## L2 Capability Areas

| L2 Capability | Description | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| **Perimeter Defense** | Inspection and filtering of north-south traffic at network boundaries through stateful firewall controls, ingress/egress policy enforcement, and threat-aware traffic screening at the edge of enterprise network segments | Defined |
| **Application Traffic Filtering** | Layer-7 inspection and filtering of HTTP/S traffic, API calls, and web application requests to detect and block application-layer attacks including OWASP Top 10 web and API attack patterns before they reach backend services | Defined |
| **Traffic Inspection and Encryption Enforcement** | Governed inspection of encrypted traffic through TLS termination and re-encryption at designated inspection points, enabling security monitoring of otherwise opaque traffic flows while preserving end-to-end encryption between trusted endpoints | Developing |
| **Network Segmentation and Microsegmentation** | Subdivision of the network fabric into isolated segments with explicit allow-list controls governing inter-segment communication, limiting lateral movement and containing the blast radius of a compromised workload | Developing |
| **Zero Trust Network Access** | Software-defined access architecture that evaluates verified identity, device posture, and contextual signals before establishing per-session, least-privilege network access — eliminating implicit trust based on network location | Developing |
| **DNS Security** | Protection of the DNS resolution layer from abuse as an exfiltration channel, command-and-control vector, and malware communication mechanism, with threat detection through DNS query and response analytics | Initial |
| **DDoS Protection** | Detection and mitigation of volumetric, protocol, and application-layer distributed denial-of-service attacks targeting enterprise internet-facing services and platform infrastructure | Defined |
| **Network Monitoring and Visibility** | Continuous capture, analysis, and correlation of network traffic metadata and flow records to establish behavioral baselines, detect anomalous communication patterns, and provide network forensic capability for incident investigation | Developing |
| **Cloud Network Security** | Architecture and governance of cloud-native network constructs — VPCs, VNets, security groups, NACLs, transit gateways, private service endpoints, and service mesh — to enforce segmentation, access control, and traffic inspection in cloud environments | Developing |
| **Traffic Control and Policy Enforcement** | Management of traffic routing, protocol enforcement, and network policy across enterprise network paths, ensuring traffic flows conform to architectural intent and that protocol violations are detected and blocked | Initial |

## Scope and Boundaries

**In Scope**: Governance of all traffic flows at the network layer — north-south and east-west — across data center, cloud, and hybrid environments; enforcement of explicit access controls at network segment boundaries; traffic inspection capabilities at designated inspection points; DNS-layer and DDoS-layer protection; network visibility and monitoring; cloud-native network security architecture

**Out of Scope**:
- Host-based firewall and endpoint security controls (see Endpoint Security capability map)
- Identity and access management (see Identity Security capability map)
- Application-layer security controls beyond WAF and API gateway (see Application Security capability map)
- Data classification, labeling, and data loss prevention at the application layer (see Data Security capability map)
- Security operations, incident detection, and response processes (see SecOps capability map)
- Physical network infrastructure and data center cabling

**Non-ABB Guardrail**: This document defines capabilities at L1/L2 only. Architecture Building Blocks, solution patterns, security controls, vendor selections, and compliance requirements are explicitly out of scope for this artifact.
